πρωτότοκος πάσης κτίσεως γεγεννημένος. καὶ τῇ ἐπαγωγῇ πλέον τοῦτο δείκνυσιν,
λέγων ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ ἐκτίσθη τὰ πάντα. εἰ δὲ μὴ ἦν πρὸ πάντων, πῶς ἐν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα
ἐκτίζετο; ὥστε τὸ πρωτότοκος οὐ κυρίως εἴληπται, ἐπεὶ ἐναντίον ἐστὶ τῷ μονογενεῖ·
φύσει γὰρ μὲν μονογενής ἐστιν ὁ μόνος πατρί, πρωτότοκος δὲ ὁ ἔχων ἄλλους
ἀδελφοὺς ὧν ἐστι πρῶτος. καὶ ἑκάτερα λαμβάνεσθαι κυρίως οὐκ ἐγχωρεῖ. ἐν αὐτῷ
δὲ εἶπεν ἐκτίσθαι τὰ πάντα, ἵνα ἀποστάντες τοῦ ἐλπίζειν εἰς ἀγγέλους, τὰς ἐλπίδας
ἔχωμεν ἐν Χριστῷ. καὶ ταύτην ἔχει τὴν αἰτίαν τῆς θεολογίας ὁ Παῦλος καὶ τοῦ
δημιουργὸν αὐτὸν δεῖξαι πάσης κτίσεως. τὸ δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀντὶ τοῦ δι' αὐτοῦ λέγεται.
Kol 1,18 Ὥσπερ πρωτότοκον πάσης κτίσεως ἔλεγεν αὐτὸν πρὸ τῆς κτίσεως ὄντα,
οὕτως πρωτότοκον ἐκ νεκρῶν πρὸ τῶν ἄλλων νεκρῶν εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν ἀναστάντα. οὐ
γὰρ ἄν τις εἴποι ὅτι ἀναστάντες οἱ νεκροὶ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες ἔσονται τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ
διὰ τοῦτο πρὸς τὸ τέλος εἴρηται· οἱ γὰρ πλείους ἁμαρτωλοὶ καὶ ἀσεβεῖς. ὥστε καὶ ἐν
τῷ προκειμένῳ ὁ χρόνος παρέλκει ὡς καὶ ἐνταῦθα. Ἵνα γένηται ἐν πᾶσι πρωτεύων.
ἐν πᾶσι, ποίοις; τοῖς κατ' οἰκονομίαν· πρῶτος γὰρ ἐν ὑπακοῇ, πρῶτος ἐν τῷ
βαπτίσματι, πρῶτος ἐν πολιτείᾳ, πρῶτος 3ἐν πάθει, πρῶτος ἐκ νεκρῶν, ὥστε εἰκότως
ἐν πᾶσι πρωτεύειν, τοῖς ἑπομένοις ἀρχὴ γεγονώς. 319,col2 Καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ
τοῦ σώματος, τῆς ἐκκλησίας. δημιουργὸς μὲν τῆς 320,col2 κτίσεως, δημιουργὸς δὲ
καὶ τῆς ἡμετέρας ἐπιστροφῆς. Ἵνα γένηται ἐν πᾶσιν αὐτὸς πρωτεύων. εἰ γὰρ κεφαλὴ
τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ πρωτότοκος ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἐν πολιτείᾳ πρῶτος, καὶ ἐν
παθήμασι πρῶτος, καὶ ἐν ὑπακοῇ πρῶτος, καὶ ἐν βαπτίσματι πρῶτος· ἐν πᾶσιν αὐτὸς
πρωτεύει κατὰ τὴν οἰκονομίαν. Kol 1,19– Τοῦτο τὴν ἀKolουθίαν ἔχει πρὸς τὸ αὐτός
ἐστι κεφαλὴ τῆς ἐκκλησίας. πλήρωμα δὲ εἶπε τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καλῶς καὶ ἤδη αὐτῷ
εἴρηται διὰ τὸ πεπληρῶσθαι αὐτὴν πνεύματος ἁγίου. φησὶ δὲ ὅτι ηὐδόκησεν ὁ
Χριστὸς πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικεῖν καὶ οὕτω δι' ἑαυτοῦ ἀποκαταλλάξαι καὶ
ἑνωποιῆσαι τὰ πάντα εἰς ἑαυτόν. Ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ἐφεσίους ἐδείκνυεν ὅτι πλήρωμα θεοῦ
ἡ ἐκκλησία λέγεται. ηὐδόκησεν οὖν ὁ θεὸς τὸ πλήρωμα ἑαυτοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὴν
ἐκκλησίαν τὴν πεπληρωμένην αὐτοῦ, ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ οἷα ἐν κεφαλῇ ἰδίᾳ οἰκῆσαι,
τοῦτ' ἔστιν αὐτῷ στοιχεῖν καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆφθαι, ἀλλὰ μὴ ἀγγέλων–ηὐδόκησε γὰρ δι'
αὐτοῦ ἀποκαταλλάξαι πάντα, οὐ δι' ἀγγέλων– καὶ γὰρ τὰ ὑπὲρ τοῦ κόσμου
κατορθώματα διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Kol 1,21–22 Καὶ διὰ τοιούτου αὐτοὺς διδάσκει ὅτι οὐκ
ἄγγελοι αὐτοὺς καταλλάξουσι τῷ θεῷ ἀλλ' ὁ υἱός· φησὶ γάρ· ἀποκατήλλαξεν ἡμᾶς
ἐν τῷ σώματι τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ. 321 Kol 1,23 Οὐ μέχρις ὑμῶν μόνον ἔφθασε τὸ
εὐαγγέλιον ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην· ἀλλ' οὐδεὶς οὐδαμοῦ
μετακεκίνηται, ἀλλὰ μένουσι πάντες ἑδραῖοι. διὸ καὶ τὰ νῦν ἀσφαλίζεσθε. Kol 1,24 Εἴ
τι, φησίν, ὑστέρημα πρὸς τὸ παθεῖν, ἀλλ' ἀναπληρῶ τὰ ὑπολειπόμενα τῶν θλίψεων
διὰ τὸν Χριστόν, χαίρω πάσχων ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν. διὰ τί δὲ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν; ὅτι διὰ τὸ
κηρύττειν αὐτοῖς ἔπασχεν. Καὶ γὰρ εἰ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῦ σώματος, τῆς
ἐκκλησίας, αἱ διὰ τῶν ἐπανισταμένων τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐπεγειρόμεναι θλίψεις
τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, Χριστοῦ θλίψεις καὶ μάλα εἰκότως ὀνομάζονται, ὁ ταῖς θλίψεσι ταύταις
ἐνευδοκιμῶν καὶ ἐναθλῶν οὐκ ἔξω σκοποῦ φήσειεν ἀνταναπληροῦν τὰ ὑστερήματα
τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Kol 1,26–27 Μυστήριον μέν ἐστιν ἡ οἰκονομία καὶ ἡ
ἐνανθρώπησις τοῦ Χριστοῦ, δόξα δὲ τοῦ μυστηρίου ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ ἐκ νεκρῶν,
πλοῦτος δὲ ὁ πολὺς ἔλεος ὁ ἐκ τῆς ἀφέσεως τοῦ βαπτίσματος, καὶ δωρεῖται τοῖς
βαπτιζομένοις τὴν ἀναγέννησιν. τίς ὁ πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης τοῦ μυστηρίου τούτου; μὴ
πτωχοί, φησί, γένησθε προστασίαις ἀγγέλων ὑποτρέχοντες. Πλοῦτος ἡμῖν, φησί,
Χριστὸς ἐδόθη. μὴ γενώμεθα πτωχοὶ εἰς ἀγγέλων προστασίας τραπέντες. Kol 2,3 Εἰ
ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ εἰσιν ἀπόκρυφοι τῆς γνώσεως θησαυροί, δῆλον ὡς οὐ δι' ἀγγέλων
μετασχεῖν αὐτῶν, ἀλλὰ δι' αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Kol 2,6–7 Εἰ καὶ τὸ περιπατῆσαι τῷ
ἐρριζῶσθαι ἐναντίον εἶναι δοκεῖ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῷ προκειμένῳ οὐκ ἐναντίον ἐστίν· δηλοῖ
γὰρ ἡμῖν πᾶσι τὸ 322 ἐρριζῶσθαι τὸ ἀσάλευτον τῆς πίστεως, τὸ δὲ ἐν Χριστῷ
περιπατεῖν τὸ ἐναργῶς τῇ αὐτῇ πολιτείᾳ κατ' ἴχνος βαδίζειν Χριστοῦ. Kol 2,9–10 Τὴν
ἐκκλησίαν λέγει ἅτε δὴ πεπληρωμένην τῆς θεότητος τοῦ πατρός. ὁ δὲ νοῦς ἐστι
τοιοῦτος· ἡ ἐκκλησία πλήρης ἐστίν, ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ δὲ κατοικεῖ σωματικῶς, τοῦτ'
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing the second form of the Colossians 1:15-17 note] ... having been begotten firstborn of all creation. And by what he adds he shows this more, saying that in him all things were created. But if he was not before all things, how were all things being created in him? So "firstborn" has not been taken in the proper sense, since it is the opposite of "only-begotten"; for by nature the only-begotten is the one who is alone to a father, but the firstborn is the one who has other brothers, of whom he is first. And it is not possible for both to be taken in the proper sense. And he said that all things were created in him so that, standing away from hoping in angels, we may have our hopes in Christ. And Paul has this cause of his speaking of (Christ's) godhead and of showing him to be creator of all creation. And "in him" is said in place of "through him."
Colossians 1:18. Just as he called him firstborn of all creation because he was before creation, so (he calls him) firstborn from the dead because he rose to incorruption before the other dead. For one would not say that when the dead have risen they will all be brothers of Christ, and that for this reason it was said with a view to the end; for the majority are sinners and ungodly. So in the passage before us too the time is superfluous, as also here. "That he may become first in all things." In all things, which? Those according to the economy: for first in obedience, first in baptism, first in way of life, first in suffering, first from the dead; so that fittingly he is first in all things, having become a beginning for those who follow.
[Second catena form, 319-320 col. 2:] "And he is the head of the body, the church." Creator of creation, and creator also of our turning back. "That he himself may become first in all things." For if (he is) head of the church and firstborn from the dead, and first in way of life, and first in sufferings, and first in obedience, and first in baptism, he himself is first in all things according to the economy.
Colossians 1:19- (open label). This has its sequence with "he is the head of the church." He called the church "fullness," as has also already been well said by him, because it has been filled with the Holy Spirit. And he says that Christ was pleased that all the fullness should dwell in him, and so through himself to reconcile and make one all things to himself. In the letter to the Ephesians he was showing that the church is called the fullness of God. So God was pleased that his own fullness, that is, the church filled by him, should dwell in Christ as in its own head, that is, should keep in line with him and hang from him, and not from angels; for he was pleased to reconcile all things through him, not through angels; for indeed the achievements on behalf of the world are through Christ.
Colossians 1:21-22. And through such (words) he teaches them that it is not angels who will reconcile them to God, but the Son; for he says: "he reconciled us in the body of his flesh."
Colossians 1:23. Not only as far as you did the gospel reach, but also into the whole inhabited world; yet no one anywhere has been moved away, but all remain settled. Therefore you too, now, make yourselves secure.
Colossians 1:24. If there is any lack, he says, regarding suffering, yet I fill up what is left of the afflictions for Christ's sake; I rejoice suffering for you. And why "for you"? Because he was suffering on account of preaching to them. For indeed, if Christ is the head of the body, the church, the afflictions raised against the church by those who rise up against the word of the truth are very fittingly named afflictions of Christ; the one who wins renown in these afflictions and contends in them would say, not outside the mark, that he fills up in his turn the lacks of the afflictions of Christ.
Colossians 1:26-27. The mystery is the economy and the becoming human of Christ; the glory of the mystery is the resurrection from the dead; the riches, the great mercy from the forgiveness of baptism, and it grants to the baptized the rebirth. What is the riches of the glory of this mystery? Do not become poor, he says, running for shelter under the patronage of angels. Christ, he says, was given to us as riches. Let us not become poor, having turned to the patronage of angels.
Colossians 2:3. If in Christ are the hidden treasures of knowledge, it is clear that (we are) to share in them not through angels but through Christ himself.
Colossians 2:6-7. Even if walking seems to be opposite to being rooted, yet in the present passage it is not opposite; for being rooted shows to all of us the unshakenness of faith, and walking in Christ (shows) clearly walking step by step in Christ's track by the same way of life.
Colossians 2:9-10. He means the church, as being filled with the godhead of the Father. The sense is this: the church is full, and it dwells in Christ bodily, that [continues in the next section: is, as a body united to a head]
pass_b_english: … begotten as the firstborn of all creation, and he shows this still more by what he adds, saying that in him all things were created. … So “firstborn” is not used in its strict sense, since it is the opposite of “only-begotten”. By nature, the only-begotten is a father’s only child, while the firstborn has other brothers and is the first of them. The two words cannot both be taken strictly. … This is Paul’s reason for speaking of Christ as God and for showing him to be the maker of all creation. …

On Colossians 1:18: He called him firstborn of all creation because he existed before creation. In the same way he calls him firstborn from the dead because he rose to incorruption before the rest of the dead. No one would say that when the dead have risen they will all be Christ’s brothers, as if the title had been given with that outcome in view; most of them are sinners and ungodly. So in the earlier verse, as in this one, the sense of time is beside the point. “That in all things he might come to have first place.” In which things? Those that belong to his saving dispensation. He was first in obedience, first in baptism, first in his way of life, first in suffering, first from the dead. So he rightly has first place in all things, since he became the beginning for those who follow him.

The second catena form adds: “And he is the head of the body, the church.” He is the maker of creation, and the maker too of our conversion. … If he is head of the church and firstborn from the dead, then he is first in all things that belong to the saving dispensation.

On Colossians 1:19–20: This follows on from “he is the head of the church”. He calls the church “fullness”, as he has already rightly said, because it has been filled with the Holy Spirit. He says that Christ was pleased to have all the fullness dwell in him, and so through himself to reconcile all things and make them one with himself. In the letter to the Ephesians he showed that the church is called the fullness of God (Ephesians 1:23). So God was pleased that his fullness, the church he has filled, should dwell in Christ as in its own head: that is, it should keep in step with Christ and depend on him, not on angels. For God was pleased to reconcile all things through Christ, not through angels. Indeed, everything achieved for the world was achieved through Christ.
On Colossians 1:21–22: In these words too he teaches them that it is not angels who will reconcile them to God, but the Son. For he says, “He reconciled us in the body of his flesh.”
On Colossians 1:23: The gospel has reached not only you but the whole world, and nowhere has anyone been moved from it; they all stand firm. So you, too, must make yourselves secure now.

On Colossians 1:24: If anything is lacking as regards suffering, he says, still I am filling up what remains of the afflictions for Christ’s sake; I rejoice to suffer for you. Why “for you”? Because he suffered for preaching to them. If Christ is the head of the body, the church, then the afflictions stirred up against the church by those who rise against the word of truth are very rightly called Christ’s afflictions. So the one who distinguishes himself in these afflictions and struggles through them would not be wide of the mark to say that he is filling up, in his turn, what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ.

On Colossians 1:26–27: The mystery is Christ’s saving dispensation and his becoming man. The glory of the mystery is the resurrection from the dead. The riches are the great mercy that comes from the forgiveness given in baptism, which also grants rebirth to the baptized. “What is the riches of the glory of this mystery?” Do not become poor, he says, by running to shelter under the patronage of angels. Christ, he says, has been given to us as our riches. Let us not become poor by turning to the patronage of angels.
On Colossians 2:3: If the hidden treasures of knowledge are in Christ, then clearly we share in them through Christ himself, not through angels.

On Colossians 2:6–7: “Walking” may seem to be the opposite of “being rooted”, but in this passage it is not. “Being rooted” shows all of us the unshakeable firmness of faith, while “walking in Christ” means following plainly in Christ’s footsteps by living the same life.
On Colossians 2:9–10: He means the church, since it has been filled with the Godhead of the Father. The sense is this: the church is full, and it dwells in Christ bodily, that …

choices.term: πρωτότοκος πάσης κτίσεως γεγεννημένος … τὸ δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀντὶ τοῦ δι' αὐτοῦ λέγεται.
choices.english: second-form continuation printed only where it adds material, with '…' for the repeated sentences
choices.why: Continues the unmarked second form of the 1:15–17 note begun at the end of u01-rem-early. Kept: 'begotten firstborn of all creation' and 'shows this more by what he adds'; the argument that 'firstborn' is not used strictly, being the opposite of 'only-begotten'; 'this is Paul's reason for speaking of him as God and showing him maker of all creation'. Dropped as repeats: 'if he was not before all things...', 'in him ... so that we hope in Christ, not angels', 'in him = through him'.

choices.term: ὥστε καὶ ἐν τῷ προκειμένῳ ὁ χρόνος παρέλκει ὡς καὶ ἐνταῦθα
choices.english: So in the earlier verse, as in this one, the sense of time is beside the point.
choices.why: Compressed sentence: 'firstborn' (1:15 and 1:18) does not imply later brothers of the same kind. Rendered close to the words; recorded as uncertain in translator_notes. The old English 'time passes just as it does here' was a misreading of παρέλκει.
rejected: time passes just as it does here (old)

choices.term: 319,col2 Καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ … κατὰ τὴν οἰκονομίαν.
choices.english: Doublet collapsed (Colossians 1:18): first form kept; second form reduced to 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Added material: the lemma 'he is the head of the body, the church', 'maker of creation and maker of our conversion', and the conclusion that being head and firstborn makes him first in everything in the economy. The list 'first in way of life, sufferings, obedience, baptism' repeats the first form and is not reprinted.
Open edition label; the note explains 'fullness' (1:19) and 'reconcile all things to himself' (1:20). SOURCE_ISSUES item 4: the old section ended on 1:19-20 with no label.

choices.term: καὶ γὰρ τὰ ὑπὲρ τοῦ κόσμου κατορθώματα διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
choices.english: Indeed, everything achieved for the world was achieved through Christ.
choices.why: The old English left this as a stray line 'the rectifications for the world' and dropped the rest of the section (1:21–2:10).

choices.term: Ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ἐφεσίους … οὐ δι' ἀγγέλων
choices.why: Restates the note with God, not Christ, as the one 'pleased'; it adds the Ephesians reference and the angels point, and the edition does not mark it as a second form, so it is kept as written.

choices.term: μὴ πτωχοί … γένησθε … μὴ γενώμεθα πτωχοὶ
choices.why: A short repeat inside one note, second time in the first person plural with the added 'Christ has been given to us as our riches'; kept as written.
